text:
leah: thinking out loud — I'm prototyping a different approach to mixed-capacity pools: keep a small persistent on-demand floor per region (like 10-15% of baseline capacity) and instead of a huge dedicated burst pool, maintain a distributed spot "buffer" that we can drain/hand off quickly for short spikes. interested in tradeoffs re: evictions, networking, and dashboarding :thinking:

sandeep: sounds reasonable. my quick mental model: min_on_demand_floor reduces risk of immediate capacity collapse during large preemption events, buffer pool reduces steady cost compared to reserving large on-demand burst. key is sizing buffer to p95 traffic and ensuring fast fallback if buffer evaporates.

leah: exactly. thinking defaults: min_on_demand_floor = 12% per region, buffer target = 1.2x p95 token throughput for 60s spikes. open to pushback.

olga: main ops caveat — network pinned resources. some of our models need EFA/connectivity to other AZ-local infra (KV cache, local shards). if buffer nodes live in different AZs or different instance families we get additional cross-AZ bandwidth and tail latency. we should tag buffer nodes with network_class and prefer same-AZ placement for critical routes.

juan: also consider eviction-rate hedging. we saw pole of 8-10% preemptions in eu-west during maintenance windows. suggest a simple hedging rule: if spot_eviction_rate_5m > 3% then automatically raise floor by +5% and reduce buffer scaling target. cheap to experiment with.

leah: @juan good call. how do folks feel about automated temporary uplift of on-demand floor vs active draining and shift-to-queue? which is less disruptive?

sandeep: uplift is smoother for live SLOs (fewer re-routes), but costs spike. draining into queue/backpressure preserves costs but increases tail latency. recommend: 1) try uplift for SLO-critical routes, 2) queue/backpressure for best-effort work. make the policy per-route.

leah: agreed. simple policy sketch:
```json
{
  "min_on_demand_floor": "12%",
  "buffer_pool": {
    "type": "spot",
    "target_headroom": "1.2x_p95",
    "max_burst_duration_s": "60"
  },
  "eviction_hedge": {
    "window_5m_threshold": "0.03",
    "floor_increment": "5%"
  },
  "fallback": {
    "critical": "raise-floor->on-demand",
    "best_effort": "drain->queue"
  }
}
```

olga: add network_class preference: prefer_same_az: true for routes with <30ms cross-AZ penalty. also add a label for instance-family-compat so we don't mix kernels that cause compilation churn on the runtime.

juan: ops hooks: when we detect buffer_eviction, run this quick drain script to preserve connections:
```
kubectl get pods -l pool=buffer -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl cordon {} && kubectl drain {} --timeout=45s --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
that's brutal for short functions but it buys ~45s of graceful KV flushes.

infra-bot: metric update — us-west-2 spot_eviction_rate_1h=0.032, avg_buffer_util=0.27, p95_latency_delta_when-evicted=120ms

leah: helpful. could we also autoscale buffer_node_type towards cheaper families when eviction rate is low and we have > 20% idle capacity? would reduce unit cost. but need guardrails so we don't degrade throughput for large contexts.

sandeep: yes — implement family_preference list with a heavy/medium/light classification. autoscaler picks light families for ephemeral inferencing (short ctx) and heavy for long context models. add a safety check: predicted_tail_latency_increase < 5% before switching family.

juan: one more note — dashboards and alerts. important to correlate: spot_eviction_rate, buffer_utilization, floor_uplifts, route_error_rate. put a synthetic traffic probe that blips 60s at p95 volume every 3h to validate burst path.

leah: plan: I'll draft a small RFC with config knobs, autoscaler changes, network tags, and alerting. will include simulated cost model: cost_with_floor = on_demand_cost * floor + spot_cost * (1-floor). want to run 2-week sim on historical demand.

olga: +1. please include a failure-mode diagram: what happens if whole region experiences 20% sustained preemptions for >10m. list manual steps.

leah: will do. thanks all — ping me if you want specific numbers or want to run sims together. :rocket:
